venues.d: Lagoon suites reached by boat, a Sense spa on its own island, and a hush that has held Forbes Five-Star status for years — the coast's most complete grand resort.

venues.n: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Riviera Maya
venues.d: Belmond's beach house on one of the Caribbean's most beautiful strands — whitewashed, thatched, deeply private, recently and beautifully restored.
Freestanding jungle-and-beach villas, a spa built around a cenote, and a kitchen led by Mexico City's Jorge Vallejo — wellness and gastronomy in one hush.
A discreet, design-led enclave on its own peninsula minutes from the airport — Forbes Five-Star, with a celebrated ESPA spa and quiet, contemporary calm.
Asian-inflected pool villas threaded through mangrove and lagoon — Banyan Tree's signature spa ritual transplanted to the Caribbean, now a Forbes Five-Star house.
A serene Auberge house raised on stilts through the mangrove to a white-sand beach — spare, elemental design and a quietly excellent kitchen.
A sleek, compact Waldorf on a fine stretch of Cancún beach — 173 rooms, a Maya-inspired spa and the assured service of the flag.
The largest of the Mayakoba houses — 401 rooms across 45 acres of jungle and lagoon, with a strong spa and a genuinely family-minded run.

venues.a: Xpu-Ha (between Playa del Carmen and Tulum)
venues.d: A former duchess's beachfront estate turned intimate hideaway — the only Three-Key hotel on this coast, and its most personal luxury.
An off-grid, solar-run beach camp inside the Sian Ka'an reserve — a handful of tented villas, wellness-led and utterly removed.
Jonatán Gómez Luna's deconstructed, theatrical Mexican tasting menu — trained through elBulli, Noma and El Celler de Can Roca, and the most ambitious kitchen on the coast.
Carlos Gaytán — the first Mexican chef to hold a Michelin star — cooks a water-themed nine-course journey through his native flavours in a jewel-box room.
Nahúm Velasco's nine-course tasting menu inside Grand Velas — the coast's rare Michelin star within an all-inclusive resort, and holder of the 2025 Service Award.
Wood-fired, jungle-chic cooking on the Tulum beach road — open flame, local produce and one of the coast's most atmospheric rooms.
Chef-driven Mexican street flavours with real technique — vivid, generous and honestly priced, a Bib Gourmand favourite off Playa's Fifth Avenue.
A tiny, home-style kitchen reinterpreting Mexican classics with the season — mole and slow-cooked dishes done with real heart.
A bright, market-led kitchen crossing Mexican produce with Asian technique — inventive, good value and a critics' Bib pick.
Sea-facing, produce-driven cooking in the sleepy fishing town between Cancún and Playa — a considered Bib Gourmand kitchen away from the crowds.
Grand Velas' ode to Mexican haute cuisine — regional classics, mezcal and a formal, romantic room beside its Michelin-starred sibling.
Rosewood's lakeside room — Mexican by day, Italian by night — with the polish and produce of a Forbes Five-Star house.
The kitchen beside Rosewood's award-winning Zapote Bar — Maya-rooted, farm-to-table cooking matched to one of the region's great drinks lists.
The wood-fired, off-grid restaurant that shaped Tulum's whole dining scene — everything cooked over open flame, the menu set by the day's catch and market.
A barefoot, beachfront Italian of homemade pasta and just-caught fish — the romantic, candlelit heart of old Tulum.
Mexico's most respected modern seafood house — ceviches, tostadas and grilled catch done with real freshness and buzz.

The only Maya city built on the sea — grey temples on a limestone cliff above a turquoise cove, El Castillo watching over the water. A photogenic, easy-walking site the whole family can do in a cool morning, then descend the wooden stairs to swim off the little beach below.

A vast, still-jungled Maya city where you pedal or take a bici-taxi between temples under the canopy. Nohoch Mul, one of the peninsula's tallest pyramids, reopened for climbing in December 2025 on a new wooden staircase — the reward at the top is an ocean of unbroken rainforest.

venues.n: Museo Maya de Cancún & the El Rey ruins
venues.d: The city's serious cultural stop, minutes from the beach resorts: a purpose-built museum of Maya artefacts paired with the small seaside El Rey ruins, where iguanas sun themselves on the platforms. An easy, air-conditioned culture fix for a day when nobody wants to travel far.

venues.n: MUSA — Museo Subacuático de Arte (underwater museum)
venues.a: Cancún / Isla Mujeres National Marine Park
venues.d: Over 500 life-size sculptures by Jason deCaires Taylor standing on the seabed, slowly turning into living reef. Snorkel the shallow Nizuc gallery, scuba the deeper Manchones one, or stay dry over a glass-bottom boat — a surreal outing that works for mixed-ability groups.

A slow, golf-cart island where Punta Sur — the easternmost point of Mexico — drops in sculpture-dotted cliffs to the Caribbean, with a small Maya shrine to Ixchel at the tip. Charter a private catamaran for the day and the family swims, lunches and watches the sunset without a crowd in sight.

Regularly named among the Caribbean's finest beaches — flour-soft white sand and water so shallow and calm you can wade out a long way, ideal for grandparents and small children alike. Claim a shaded bed at a beach club and let the afternoon dissolve.

One of the most beautiful open-and-cavern cenotes — crystalline freshwater over pale rock, with turtles and small fish, and stalactite chambers you can snorkel into. A gentle, unforgettable introduction to the underworld the Maya held sacred.

"Two Eyes" — twin sapphire pools opening into one of the world's great flooded cave systems, superb for both easy snorkelling and world-class cavern diving. A private guide can tailor it from a splash for the children to a proper cave dive for the certified.
A vast, deep, startlingly blue open cenote on the shore of the Bacalar lagoon, ringed by jungle and a laid-back restaurant deck. The plunge into cool, clear water is a highlight of any Bacalar day.

venues.n: Ruta de los Cenotes, Puerto Morelos
venues.d: A jungle road strung with dozens of cenotes — open pools, cavern swims, zip-lines and rope swings — far less trafficked than the Tulum circuit. A private driver lets you pick two or three, from a serene swim for elders to an adventure stop for teenagers.

venues.a: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.d: A polished, all-day park built around underground rivers, wildlife, and a genuinely spectacular evening show of Mexican music, dance and history. Multi-generational catnip — small children, teenagers and grandparents all find their own version of the day.

A calm natural inlet where the freshwater river meets the sea — snorkelling among fish in glass-clear water, gentle floats and cliff jumps, with food and drink included. The most relaxed of the eco-parks, easy on non-swimmers and older travellers.

venues.a: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.d: The high-adrenaline sibling — long zip-line circuits, amphibious vehicles through the jungle, and swimming and rafting through stalactite-hung underground rivers. The park teenagers and thrill-seeking adults will remember longest.

The Riviera's stylish heart — a long pedestrian avenue of boutiques, mezcalerías and rooftop restaurants a block back from the sand. An easy evening of strolling, shopping and dinner, with the Cozumel ferry leaving from its pier.

A small, unspoilt fishing town between Cancún and Playa, with a leaning lighthouse, good seafood and a protected national-park reef just offshore. The most authentic, low-key village base within easy reach of the airport.

"Place of the Turtles" — a sheltered bay where green sea turtles graze on seagrass in waist-deep water, snorkelled with a licensed guide. A wildlife encounter that reliably thrills children and adults, best booked early with a private guide to avoid the day-tripper rush.

"Where the sky is born" — a million-plus acres of mangrove, lagoon and reef where you float the ancient Maya canals, spot dolphins, turtles and hundreds of birds. A private boat safari here is the wild, pristine counterpoint to the resort coast.

venues.n: Cancún Hotel Zone beaches & Nichupté Lagoon
venues.d: The famous 22-kilometre strip of white Caribbean sand backed by the calm Nichupté Lagoon on its inner side — swimming, catamaran sailing and sunset cruises without leaving the resort corridor. The effortless default for a day when the family just wants sea and sand.

venues.n: Private yacht or catamaran charter, Cancún–Isla Mujeres
venues.d: The signature UHNI day here — a crewed yacht to Isla Mujeres for swimming, snorkelling the reef and an anchored lunch, entirely on your own timetable. Add a chef and it becomes the trip's most memorable, most private afternoon.

The ancient Maya steam-lodge ritual, led by a shaman with herbs, chanting and darkness — a cleansing, ceremonial experience quite unlike a spa. A grounding, spiritual counterpoint to the beach, and one many Indian travellers find deeply resonant.

A guided flight through Mexico's agave spirits, from crisp blanco tequilas to smoky artisanal mezcals, with a sommelier explaining terroir and craft. A sophisticated evening for the adults while the children are looked after at the resort.

venues.n: Luxury beach clubs of the Riviera Maya
venues.d: Design-led beach clubs — daybeds, ceviche, cocktails and a DJ over the turquoise water — from Tulum's boho-chic scene to Playa's polished spots. The stylish, low-effort way to spend a whole day on the sand in comfort.

venues.a: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.d: A guided wade and float through a half-flooded cave of stalactites and mirror-still water, helmet-lamps lighting formations older than the Maya. A cool, awe-inspiring hour underground that even nervous swimmers can do in a life vest.

"Heaven" — a shallow, sandy-bottomed sandbar where dozens of starfish rest in impossibly clear water, best reached by private boat from Cozumel. A gentle, magical snorkel that suits families and non-divers.

venues.a: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.d: A 300-strong cast telling the story of Mexico through pre-Hispanic ball games, charro horsemanship, regional dance and mariachi in a vast open-air theatre. The single most crowd-pleasing evening in the region for a multi-generational group.

Beneath the ruins runs one of the Caribbean's most beautiful beaches — powder sand, palms and warm shallow water at Playa Paraíso. Combine an early ruins visit with a long swim below the temples for the classic Tulum morning.

A serene turquoise lagoon ringed by a darker central cenote plunging deep into the earth, far quieter than the beach. A calm, photogenic swim and float away from the crowds, easy to fold into a Tulum day.

World-class waters — offshore for sailfish, marlin and mahi-mahi from Cancún, and the flats of Ascension Bay for bonefish, tarpon and permit. A private crewed charter tailors the day from trophy fishing to a gentle family reef troll.

venues.n: Kite-surfing & watersports at Puerto Morelos / Tulum
venues.d: Steady Caribbean trade winds make this coast excellent for kite-surfing, paddleboarding and sailing, with private instructors for beginners. An active morning for the sportier members of the group while others linger over breakfast.

venues.n: Cenote Dos Ojos to Cenote Nicte-Ha, Sac Actun
venues.d: The Sac Actun system is among the longest underwater cave networks on earth, and Nicte-Ha's lily-covered surface makes a serene, easy snorkel beside the more famous Dos Ojos. A quieter, lovelier pairing for those who want the cenotes without the crowds.
Rosewood Mayakoba's jungle-set cocktail bar — Maya-inspired, farm-to-glass drinks built on Mexican distillates, ranked for years among the continent's best.
The Saint-Tropez French-Mediterranean import on Tulum beach — rosé, long lunches and a glossy, high-energy day-into-night scene.
Rosa Negra group's beach club — Mediterranean plates, sax-and-violin 'happenings' and Tulum's signature sundown party energy.
Pan-Latin sharing plates, live percussion and sparkler-lit tables — the group's flagship beach club and one of Tulum's most-booked nights.
Cancún's legendary mega-club — acrobats, tribute acts and non-stop spectacle, the definitive high-octane night in the Hotel Zone.
The Waldorf Astoria's poised beachfront bar — considered cocktails and Caribbean views in one of Cancún's most refined new houses.
